sections.heading: Choose a Problem
sections.body: Pick a real problem—ideally one you care about. Write a one-sentence promise: what is the tiniest transformation the product achieves? This promise becomes the north star for all design and engineering decisions.

sections.heading: Write the Story
sections.body: Create a 30-second first-run narrative. Write it as if narrating a video. Mark beats and call out signals the user will see or hear. Keep it lightweight so it stays alive through iterations.

sections.heading: Design the Loops
sections.body: List loops for create, edit, delete, and share. Assign timing budgets and repair paths. Establish which loops can be optimistic and which require confirmation due to risk.

sections.heading: Build the Scene
sections.body: Wireframe a scene with clear props and a dominant verb. Use progressive disclosure for complexity. Decide where motion helps orientation and where it distracts.

sections.heading: Instrument and Iterate
sections.body: Add observability for beats and loops. Run a small test with real users. Adjust copy, timing, and defaults. Keep the story updated. Ship a coherent vibe at each milestone.

sections.heading: Share the Craft
sections.body: Teach your team the vocabulary. Add a vibe section to specs and PRs. Celebrate small wins. Vibe coding is a craft; it improves with practice and generosity.
